info.title: LP Ranger API
info.description: REST API for the LP Ranger auto-rebalancing concentrated liquidity manager. Manages V3 NFT positions on 9mm Pro (PulseChain).

tags.name: UI
tags.description: Static JSON the dashboard fetches at init: shipped defaults, provider metadata, and display labels.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description: Encrypted third-party credentials (Moralis). Keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest and never returned by any endpoint.

tags.name: Telegram
tags.description: Telegram bot credentials and per-event notification toggles. Credentials are stored encrypted and only their presence is reported back.

tags.name: Price Lookups
tags.description: Idle-driven pause for quota-limited USD price endpoints.

get.description: Returns 200 OK with server port and timestamp. Used by load balancers and process managers.
Returns global server state and per-position bot state. Polled every 3 seconds by the dashboard.

rpcUrl.description: The endpoint currently in use — the live primary, which changes the moment an operator adds or promotes one. Not the value resolved at startup.

startingManagedPositions.description: While the server starts the positions saved as managed, one at a time after a launch: how many it has dealt with (`done`) and how many there are (`total`). Null at any other time. The dashboard's badge reads Syncing while it is set.

positions.description: Per-position state keyed by composite key (blockchain-wallet-contract-tokenId)

post.description: Update global or per-position config. Position-specific keys require a positionKey (composite key validated by parseCompositeKey).

positionKey.description: Composite key (blockchain-wallet-contract-tokenId). Required for position-specific keys.

impermanentLossGuardPct.description: Impermanent Loss Guard, percent. Per position. Range: impermanentLossGuardPct in setting-bounds.json.

rangeOverrideEnabled.description: Bot Configuration > Range "No Override" toggle. false = re-use the position's existing on-chain range on the next rebalance and ignore the three Range settings below.

rebalanceRangeWidthPct.description: Price Range Extension: half-width of the new range as a percent of the current price. Ignored while rangeOverrideEnabled is false.

fullRangeRebalanceEnabled.description: Mint the next rebalance across the full tick range. Ignored while rangeOverrideEnabled is false.

offsetToken0Pct.description: Position offset bias toward token0; 50 is balanced.

slippagePctToken0.description: Slippage tolerance, percent, for swaps whose DESTINATION token is token0. Unset falls back to the shipped slippagePct default in bot-config-defaults.json. Honoured by rebalances and compounds alike.

slippagePctToken1.description: Slippage tolerance, percent, for swaps whose DESTINATION token is token1. Unset falls back to the shipped slippagePct default in bot-config-defaults.json. Honoured by rebalances and compounds alike.

lifetimeStartDateOverrideUtc.description: ISO-8601 UTC date. Overrides the detected start of the lifetime window.

decimalsOverride0.description: Manual decimals for token0, when on-chain detection fails.

decimalsOverrideForce0.description: Apply decimalsOverride0 even when on-chain detection succeeded.

decimalsOverrideForce1.description: Apply decimalsOverride1 even when on-chain detection succeeded.

rpcUrls.description: GLOBAL. JSON-RPC endpoints added by the operator, most recently added first. The first entry is the primary; the endpoints shipped in chains.json stay behind them as failover. Applied immediately, without a restart.

approvalMultiple.description: GLOBAL. ERC-20 approval multiplier for swap allowances.

gasFeePct.description: GLOBAL. The swap gas gate: a swap whose gas would cost more than this percent of the swap's own value is skipped, in a rebalance or a compound. Range: gasFeePct in setting-bounds.json.

priceCacheTtlMs.description: GLOBAL. In-memory token-price cache TTL, ms.

dustUnitPriceCacheMultiplier.description: GLOBAL. Dust-unit-price TTL as a multiple of priceCacheTtlMs.

moveCacheTtlMs.description: GLOBAL. Cache TTL for the fresh-price window around a rebalance or compound.

pricePauseExceptionPollWindowMultiple.description: GLOBAL. Poll cycles between the balanced-band notifier fresh-price probes.

moralisEnabled.description: GLOBAL. Whether the stored Moralis API key is used for price lookups. Independent of whether a key exists: false stops the calls without discarding the key. Default true.

200.description: Config saved. An answer to a request that named a position names it too: positionKey is the key the request named, and livePositionKey the key the values were saved under when a rebalance had moved it, so a dashboard that has moved to another position since it asked can keep the answer off its screen.

400.description: Missing or invalid positionKey for position-specific keys, or a dashboard-settable value outside its range. The route takes settings only: the bot's own records (hodlBaseline, residuals, compoundHistory and the rest) are not saved through it. The two refusals are told apart by the response's invalidValueForKey field, which names the setting whose value was refused and is absent on a malformed request. Values are refused, never corrected, and nothing in the request is applied. Ranges are declared in src/lib/config-bounds.js; null clears a setting rather than being checked. Names the position as the 200 does.

get.description: Returns whether a wallet is loaded, its address, and lock state.

post.description: Decrypt the wallet file and the stored api keys with the provided password. The first unlock also starts the positions saved as managed; the request is idempotent, so entering the password again only confirms it.
Import a wallet via seed phrase or private key. Encrypts and persists to app-config/user-configurable/wallet.json.

409.description: Refused, with nothing imported: an import stops every position and starts the saved ones again, so it waits while the server is still starting the positions saved as managed, and is refused once the server is stopping. `error` says which, in the operator's words.

delete.description: Delete the encrypted wallet file from disk.

post.description: Decrypt and return the plaintext private key. Requires password.
Enumerate up to 300 NFT and ERC-20 LP positions for the loaded wallet. Results are cached.
Re-read on-chain liquidity for previously scanned positions.

get.description: Returns all positions currently managed by the bot with their status.

True when the server manages the position the key names: its bot loop runs, or its saved status is running and the loop has not started yet. False for a position a shutdown has just stopped. The dashboard asks on every position switch and draws the Manage/Stop button from it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The position's composite key, chain-wallet-contract-tokenId, addresses EIP-55 checksummed.

400.description: The key is missing or names no position

post.description: Start a bot loop for the specified NFT position. Requires a loaded wallet with a private key.

200.description: Position started. Names it by positionKey, and by livePositionKey too when a re-open's first rebalance minted it a new NFT before the answer; a refusal after the key is known names it by positionKey.

400.description: Missing tokenId or no private key

409.description: Nothing was started, for one of three reasons. LP Ranger manages one active position per liquidity pool, so that profit and loss stays attributable to it. `pool-already-managed`: another position already manages this pool, and the body names it. `pool-has-open-position`: the position is closed, so its Manage would re-open it, and the wallet already holds an open position in its pool, which the body names; the wallet's positions are those the last wallet scan saw open, each still open unless the chain answers otherwise. Or nothing may start now: the server is still starting the positions saved as managed, one of which may be in the same pool, or it is stopping; the body then carries only `ok` and `error`. A re-open retried on a running position (`forceRebalance: true`) while a scan is running on it is refused too, since its rebalance would be left out of the figures the scan rebuilds; `error` then asks for Manage again once the read finishes, and the body names the position by positionKey.

error.description: `pool-already-managed`, `pool-has-open-position`, or, in the operator's words, why nothing may start now, naming the start-up's progress while it runs.

openTokenId.description: With `pool-has-open-position`: NFT id of the open position the wallet holds in the pool.

conflictTokenId.description: With `pool-already-managed`: NFT id of the running position holding the pool.

positionKey.description: Composite key of the position refused, as every answer about a position names it.

503.description: Nothing was started, since the chain could not be read: `pool-info-unavailable`. Either the position's pool, without which LP Ranger cannot check that no other position is managed in it, or the pool's state, which the bot reads as it starts. `message` says which. Try again in a moment.

message.description: What could not be read, in the operator's words.

tokenId.description: NFT id of the position refused.

positionKey.description: Composite key of the position refused, as every answer about a position names it.

delete.description: Stop the bot loop for a position. Sets status to 'stopped' but keeps config data.

200.description: Position stopped. Names it by positionKey, the key sent, and by livePositionKey too when a rebalance moved it during the stop.

post.description: Fast fetch of pool state, token prices, value, composition, and current P&L for an unmanaged position.

200.description: Position details with pool state, value, and P&L

post.description: Slow fetch: event scan + epoch reconstruction for historical P&L data. May take several minutes on first call (cold cache).

200.description: Lifetime P&L with daily breakdown, gas costs, and rebalance events

get.description: Fetch historical P&L data for a closed (drained) NFT position.

200.description: Historical P&L for the closed position

post.description: Trigger a manual rebalance for a managed position. Its range comes from the position's saved Range settings (Bot Configuration > Range) while rangeOverrideEnabled is true; otherwise the existing range is re-used, re-centred on the price. No width is accepted on this endpoint.

200.description: Rebalance requested. Names the position by positionKey.

409.description: Position not running, or a scan is running on it: a rebalance made during the scan would be left out of the figures it rebuilds. The scan refusal carries `scanInProgress: true` and the reason in `error`; the dashboard's dialog waits for the scan to end. Names the position by positionKey. Once accepted, the rebalance holds the position's scans back until it is made.

post.description: Collect unclaimed fees and reinvest as liquidity on the same NFT position.

409.description: Position not running, or a scan is running on it: a compound made during the scan would be left out of the figures it rebuilds. The scan refusal carries `scanInProgress: true`, the reason in `error`, and the position's positionKey; the dashboard's Compound Now dialog waits for the scan to end. Once accepted, the compound holds the position's scans back until it is made.

post.summary: Stop the server once nothing is under way
post.description: A stop the server holds until nothing it has under way is left. From the first request the server starts nothing new: no position starts, no check begins a rebalance or compound, and Reload Current Position and Re-scan Prices are refused. It exits once each rebalance or compound under way, and then each scan still running, has finished, however long that takes; the shutdown alert goes out as it does on Ctrl+C. A repeat changes nothing and answers what the stop still waits for. `npm run gentle-stop`, the recommended stop, sends it every two seconds and prints the answer. Ctrl+C and `npm stop` exit within three seconds, cutting a move or scan off.

200.description: The stop is held. What it still waits for, position by position.

position.description: The pair and NFT, as the log names it.

get.description: The dashboard settings the server sends: app-config/app-defaults-for-user-configurable/ui-defaults_non-layout_for-server-up-scenario.json, with the operator's copy in app-config/user-configurable/ on top. Read once at startup, which stops on a value outside its range in setting-bounds.json or outside the timer rule. The dashboard asks for them after the blockchain and before its first poll. Defaults are in docs/configuration.md.

200.description: Every setting the file holds, with its value in force

dashboardPollIntervalMs.description: How often the dashboard asks for fresh figures, in milliseconds.

staleDataCheckIntervalMs.description: How often the dashboard checks whether the figures it shows are still another position's, in milliseconds.

reloadMaxWaitMs.description: How long Reload Current Position waits for its scan before reloading the page anyway, in milliseconds.

slippageConfirmAbovePct.description: A per-token slippage saved above this percentage asks for a click on Confirm.

slippageTypedConfirmFromPct.description: A per-token slippage saved at or above this percentage asks for Confirm to be typed.

pollSkipLogEvery.description: While a slow server holds a poll, the console gets one line per this many skipped polls.

lastCheckJustNowSec.description: How long Mission Control's last-check tag reads "just now", in seconds.

autoCompoundSyncHoldMs.description: How long after Stop Managing the status polls leave the Auto-Compound toggle alone, in milliseconds.

throttleNearLimitPct.description: The share of Max Rebalances / Day, in percent, at which the throttle badge reads NEAR LIMIT.

activityLogMaxEntries.description: How many entries the Activity Log keeps.

copyFeedbackMs.description: How long a copy icon shows that it copied, in milliseconds.

heapLogIntervalMs.description: How often the dashboard logs its heap size to the browser console, in milliseconds.

soundsEnabled.description: Whether sounds play, for a browser with no saved choice.

privacyModeEnabled.description: Whether Privacy Mode is on, for a browser with no saved choice.

privacyBlurWalletAddresses.description: Whether Privacy Mode blurs wallet addresses, for a browser with no saved choice.

privacyBlurUsdAmounts.description: Whether Privacy Mode blurs USD amounts above the threshold, and coin amounts, for a browser with no saved choice.

privacyUsdAmountThreshold.description: The USD amount Privacy Mode blurs above, for a browser with no saved choice.

get.description: Returns the contents of app-config/app-defaults-for-user-configurable/lp-providers.json — LP-provider metadata keyed by <poolFactoryAddress>_<positionManagerAddress> in EIP-55 checksum casing. Each entry is an object { displayName: string, supportedBlockchainsByLpRangerAndLpProvider: string[] } where supportedBlockchainsByLpRangerAndLpProvider is a list of canonical chain IDs (KEYs of chains.json, e.g. "pulsechain") that we've verified for that deployment.

The Bot Configuration defaults, resolved as the bot resolves them: the shipped app-config/app-defaults-for-user-configurable/bot-config-defaults.json, the operator's copy in app-config/user-configurable/ on top, and `.env` on top of both for the settings it can set. It covers every Bot Configuration input and the server-internal groups. A position's own values, which these stand in for, live in app-config/user-configurable/bot-config.json. Always 200.

The configured numbers and names the help and User Manual quote, worded for a sentence ("15", "4 hours"), from the values this install runs on: the shipped settings, with the operator's overrides and then `.env` on top. The names are the chain's and its aggregator's, from chains.json; `aggregatorName` is empty on a chain with no aggregator, and `aggregatorInUse` reads "none" there. Ranges come from the shipped setting-bounds.json alone. Also returns the Bot Configuration defaults behind them. The dashboard asks at startup until answered; the User Manual the app serves asks on load. Always 200.

200.description: The figures and the defaults behind them.

figures.description: Figure name to wording, plain text, no markup.

get.description: Serves app-config/app-defaults-for-user-configurable/setting-labels.json. The dashboard uses it to render Activity Log "Setting Saved" entries as a label plus unit instead of a raw key. Always 200 — a missing or malformed file yields an empty map and the client falls back to the raw key.

200.description: Label map keyed by config key.

get.description: Names the chains.json entry this process runs against — `CHAIN_NAME`, or `defaults.chain` in app-runtime.json. The dashboard reads it once at startup, before it builds any position key or url, because the chain is the first segment of both. Always 200.

200.description: The active chain: its id, what the header's chain link shows, and where its token logos are listed.

chainId.description: Key of the chains.json entry, e.g. `pulsechain` or `pulsechain-testnet`.

homepage.description: The chain's website, which the dashboard header's chain link opens.

logo.description: File name under src/client/web/ of the chain's logo, shown in the dashboard header.

tokenListUrl.description: Url of the chain's token list (chains.json → tokenList.url), in the Uniswap token list format; the dashboard shows each token's logoURI beside its name. Empty for a chain with no list.

get.description: Serves the tracked chart-provider list the Pool Details dialog links out to. Always 200; an unreadable file yields an empty list and the dialog renders no links rather than blocking.

Serves the active chain's RPC endpoints, most-preferred first, so the dashboard's Network section is built from configuration rather than hardcoded in markup. The list is the same one failover walks, so it cannot advertise an endpoint the bot would not use. `saved` is reported separately because the Add RPC dialog prepends to the operator's own list only — sending it the composed list would copy the shipped endpoints into saved config, where they would stop tracking chains.json. Always 200; an empty `endpoints` list means none are configured.

200.description: Ordered endpoint list, plus the operator-added subset.

endpoints.description: Every endpoint, in the order failover walks them.

primary.description: True for the endpoint currently in use. Exactly one entry is true, and it is the first.

saved.description: Endpoints the operator added via Add RPC, most recently added first. Excludes the endpoints shipped in chains.json. Empty on a fresh install.

post.description: Encrypts the key to app-config/user-configurable/api-keys.json (AES-256-GCM). A Moralis key is validated with a live ping after saving; the ping result is logged, not returned. Falls back to the wallet session password when password is omitted.

password.description: Wallet password. Optional when the wallet is already unlocked this session.

400.description: service, key, and password are required.

get.description: Reports whether a Moralis key is present and usable. "none" = no key stored; "locked" = stored but the wallet has not been unlocked this session, so it cannot be decrypted; "disabled" = stored but Use Moralis Key is off, so it is not checked; "unsupported" = stored, but the active chain has no Moralis id or wrapped native token in chains.json, so Moralis is not asked about it; "valid" = the live ping succeeded; "quota" = the key is valid but its daily quota is spent; "invalid" = the live ping failed. Always 200, including on ping failure.

Never returns the token or chat ID — only whether each is stored. balancedThresholdPct and balancedCooldownMs surface code-only constants from balanced-notifier.js so the dashboard can render the checkbox label percent and cadence without a second literal.

post.description: Each field is optional. botToken and chatId are encrypted at rest and require a password (or an unlocked wallet session); enabledEvents is written to the bot-config global section and needs neither. enabledEvents may name only alerts LP Ranger sends, each true or false, and leaving it out keeps the saved choices. A request refused for either reason saves nothing.

password.description: Required only when saving botToken or chatId.

400.description: Password required for credential fields, or enabledEvents names an alert LP Ranger does not send or holds a value other than true or false. Nothing is saved.

post.description: Sends a message through the configured bot to verify credentials end to end.

Posted by the browser after 15 minutes without input. Price endpoints are quota-limited, so the dashboard stops asking for fresh prices while nobody is watching. A rebalance or compound bypasses the pause for its own duration. Also resets the server-side idle countdown.
Posted on the next throttled activity event after an idle pause.

post.summary: Check whether a drained position can be re-opened
post.description: Reads both token balances from the wallet and compares each against the live dust threshold. Re-opening needs at least one non-dust balance. Returns 503 with a structured code when the wallet balance cannot be read right now, which the dashboard renders as a try-again-later message rather than a failure.

200.description: Decision plus the balances behind it.

400.description: Wallet not loaded, or token0/token1 missing.

post.description: Clears the position's error and pause state and asks its bot loop to run a fresh cycle. Rejected while a rebalance or scan is already in flight. liveKey is the resolved composite key, which may differ from the one sent if a rebalance minted a new tokenId in the meantime.

409.description: Refused, the position left as it was. error names why: server-stopping (the server holds a stop), scan-in-progress (a scan of the position is running), or coin-move-under-way (a rebalance or compound of the position has started, from its first gate to its end, or a Rebalance Now or Compound Now waits to be made). message is for the operator; for coin-move-under-way it reads "A coin move (rebalance or compound) for this position has already started. Try again once it's complete."

post.summary: Re-value a position at freshly fetched prices
post.description: Asks the position's next lifetime scan to rebuild every stored dollar figure at freshly fetched prices: Fees Compounded, the lifetime deposit, and the HODL baseline's entry value. The token amounts behind them are re-read from the chain but never re-derived from the pool's history, which is what makes this cheaper than a reload. Nothing is deleted: each figure is overwritten once its replacement exists, so a scan that fails leaves the old figure in place. Only a managed position has a running bot loop to pick the re-scan up, so an unmanaged one is rejected with 409 "not-managed" rather than silently doing nothing.

includeDailyPnl.description: Also re-price the Per-Day P&L table — every closed period's gas and both pair-token prices. A closed period keeps its dollar figures but not the token amounts behind them, so this re-reads each NFT's history: minutes on a long rebalance chain. Still skips the five-year pool scan that Reload Current Position performs.

limitToRecentDays.description: Rebuild only the most recent periods of the Per-Day P&L table, leaving older rows with the figures they already hold. A flag, not a day count: the window length is the rescanPricesRecentWindowDays shipped default, so a request cannot ask for a reach the dashboard never offered. Ignored without includeDailyPnl, since nothing else this route re-values is date-scoped. Ignored too when the table is incomplete, because a stored period does not record which NFT it came from, so a partial rebuild cannot tell a gap from an old period.

409.description: Refused, the position left as it was. error names why: not-managed (Re-scan Prices applies only to a managed position), server-stopping, scan-in-progress, or coin-move-under-way, as for POST /api/position/reload. message is for the operator.

post.description: Aborts the 5-year event scan for one pool. aborted reports whether a scan was actually running; flagReset reports whether the position's scan-in-progress flag was cleared, which is what re-enables Reload Current Position. positionKey is resolved to the live key first, since the dashboard may hold a key that a parallel rebalance has already migrated.

positionKey.description: Optional. Clears the scan-in-progress flag as well.

walletAddress.description: Optional. Defaults to the loaded wallet.
